hypothesis: Any substantive weakening of the governance policy (thresholds, axes, noise, ladder) changes its SHA-256 policy hash and is thus visible against the locked reference, while semantics-preserving re-serializations do not change the hash (no meta-level false alarm).
observable: policy-hash tamper detection rate and false-tamper rate

tamper_detail.name: raise_authority_tau
tamper_detail.description: authority threshold 0.125->0.30 lets true 1-step privilege escalations pass

tamper_detail.name: relax_consequence_tau
tamper_detail.description: consequence threshold 0.40->0.95 lets irreversible-assumption injections pass

tamper_detail.name: widen_scope_tau
tamper_detail.description: scope threshold 0.25->0.90 lets gross out-of-scope creep pass

tamper_detail.name: drop_authority_axis
tamper_detail.description: removes the authority_escalation axis entirely from evaluation

tamper_detail.name: widen_noise
tamper_detail.description: scope noise sigma 0.08->0.30 raises the material floor and hides real creep

tamper_detail.name: collapse_ladder
tamper_detail.description: flattens admin/root to write so escalations register zero distance

tamper_detail.name: shrink_child_weight
tamper_detail.description: child_weight 0.15->0.0 in the frozen scope definition

threshold: HOLD if policy hash not deterministic; else PASS iff tamper_detection_rate == 1.0 and false_tamper_rate == 0.0; else FAIL
honest_scope: synthetic, de-identified request/action corpus with ground-truth labels; validates the Intent-Fidelity Divergence primitive and preregistered thresholds on controlled data; NOT a live-LLM study and NOT a claim about any deployed model's behavior
